name: Bilbao
title: Bilbao Ship Thickness Gauging | UTM on the Bay of Biscay
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Bilbao for tankers, ro-ro and bulk ships: hull structure UTM, pre-docking survey readings and renewal survey gauging.
h1: Port of Bilbao UTM: Hull Thickness Gauging for Tankers, Bulkers and Ro-Ro
intro: Bilbao is the main deep-water port of Spain's Atlantic north coast, serving a refinery, an LNG terminal, the steel and engineering industries of the Basque Country and ro-ro links to the UK and Ireland. Ships here face the Bay of Biscay's weather on most passages, and their structure shows it. Our ultrasonic thickness gauging technicians are mobilised from India to Bilbao for tankers, bulk carriers, ro-ro ships and gas carriers, working at the berth or at a repair yard on the northern coast.

highlights.p: Ships trading across the Bay of Biscay take heavy weather often. We combine gauging with magnetic particle testing at hatch corners, bracket toes and frame ends, the details where weather damage tends to show first.

Bilbao's refinery, regasification terminal and steel trade bring tankers, gas carriers and bulk carriers alongside for workable stays. Gauging is planned within each terminal's permit rules and around the cargo programme.
Readings taken alongside in Bilbao can feed straight into a docking at a yard on the northern Spanish coast, with the same technicians returning to complete measurements once the ship is dry.

port.h: The Port of Bilbao: refinery, LNG, steel and Atlantic ro-ro
p: The Port of Bilbao has largely moved from the city's riverside quays to the outer harbour at the mouth of the Nervión estuary, the Abra, where breakwaters shelter deep-water berths at Santurtzi and Zierbena. Ships no longer pass the centre of the city; the old shipbuilding and dock areas upstream have been redeveloped, and most commercial calls now take place in the outer harbour, where weather rather than river traffic decides the working conditions. Liquid bulk is a large part of the traffic: crude tankers supply the Petronor refinery at Muskiz, product and chemical tankers use the energy berths, and LNG carriers call at the Bahía de Bizkaia Gas regasification terminal.

Dry bulk and general cargo reflect the Basque industrial base: steel products, scrap and other bulk move through the port for the region's steelworks and engineering firms. Container lines serve the CSP Bilbao terminal with short-sea, feeder and some deep-sea services, and ro-ro and ro-pax ships run to the UK, Ireland and northern Europe, including Brittany Ferries' Portsmouth service. Much of this is short-sea shipping on the Atlantic coast, crossing the Bay of Biscay week in, week out.

That pattern shapes inspection demand. Ships that work the Biscay coast take heavy weather regularly, and its effects — fatigue cracking at bracket toes and hatch corners, wastage in ballast tanks that are filled and emptied often, and mechanical damage to shell and decks — can appear earlier than on ships in sheltered trades. Liner ro-ro and ferry tonnage keeps tight schedules, so gauging is fitted into lay-overs and planned maintenance, while bulk carriers and tankers discharging at the outer harbour offer berth stays that suit tank and deck surveys. The northern coast's long shipbuilding tradition means repair capacity in the region, and work started alongside can continue in a yard.

facilities.h: Gauging locations in the outer harbour and along the coast
p: Most work in Bilbao happens alongside in the outer harbour. Tankers at the energy berths are gauged under the terminal's permit-to-work regime, with deck, pump room and ballast tank readings taken during cargo operations and cargo tanks measured only when gas-free. Bulk carriers discharging steel or scrap allow hold and tank access once cargo is clear, and longer discharges give time for systematic readings on hold frames, hopper tanks and transverse bulkheads. LNG carriers at the regasification terminal follow that terminal's own boarding rules, and requests there are limited to hull, ballast tank, deck and piping readings.

Ro-ro and ro-pax ships on the UK and Ireland services are gauged during lay-overs or scheduled maintenance, with vehicle decks, stern and side ramps, ballast tanks and the fire main as the usual subjects. For drydock work, the Basque and Cantabrian coasts have shipbuilders and repairers on several estuaries, and an owner can combine afloat readings in Bilbao with a later docking without changing gauging teams. Winter weather in the Bay of Biscay can delay arrivals and halt outer-harbour operations for short periods, so schedules between late autumn and early spring carry some margin. The gauges and magnetic particle yokes are portable and travel with the technicians as personal equipment.
list: Energy berths in the outer harbour — deck, pump room, ballast tank and piping gauging on crude, product and chemical tankers under terminal permits
Bahía de Bizkaia Gas terminal — readings of shell plating, segregated ballast tanks and deck lines on LNG carriers while they discharge, under terminal rules
Dry bulk and steel quays at Santurtzi and Zierbena — hold frame, hopper tank and ballast tank readings on bulkers and general cargo vessels
CSP Bilbao container terminal — scrubber piping and engine-room tank gauging on feeder and short-sea container ships during cargo work
Ro-ro and ferry berths — vehicle deck plating, ramp hinges and framing, ballast tanks and fire main lines gauged on UK and Ireland services between sailings
Shipyards on the Basque and Cantabrian coasts — docking-survey gauging where work started alongside in Bilbao is completed in dry dock

context.h: Atlantic coast rules: PSC, sulphur and EU climate measures
p: No SOx ECA currently applies in the Bay of Biscay, so at sea the global sulphur limit governs, but EU rules require low-sulphur fuel at berth in Spanish ports, and ships heading north enter the North Sea ECA at the western approaches to the English Channel. Scrubber-fitted ships on Biscay routes therefore run their systems hard on the northern legs of their rotations, and wash-water piping on short-sea ro-ro and container ships trading between Spain and northern Europe is a regular inspection subject even though Bilbao itself sits outside an ECA.

Spain's Paris MoU obligations are discharged in Bilbao by the port's Capitanía Marítima, whose inspectors see a high share of short-sea and older tonnage on these routes. Emissions obligations under EU ETS, applied to shipping from 2024, and FuelEU Maritime, from 2025, weigh heavily on ferry and short-sea operators whose rotations run between EU ports and the UK. Many of those operators are renewing or retrofitting tonnage; gauging an older ship before a sale, a conversion or a decision on life extension gives the owner the structural facts the decision depends on, rather than an estimate built from the last survey report.

jobs.h: Common gauging requests at the Port of Bilbao
jobs.p: Bilbao's requests are shaped by industrial cargo and Atlantic weather. Tankers and bulk carriers bring survey-related work during cargo stays, ro-ro and ferry operators bring planned programmes, and older short-sea ships bring condition gauging tied to sales and life-extension decisions. Each job is scoped with the superintendent before the team travels from India, and where crack detection is likely to be needed, magnetic particle equipment comes too. Typical jobs include:
list: Thickness gauging of cargo hold frames, hopper tanks and topside tanks on a bulk carrier discharging steel scrap at the outer harbour, ahead of its intermediate survey.
Magnetic particle testing at hatch corners and side shell frame ends on a general cargo ship after heavy-weather damage in the Bay of Biscay, with gauging of the surrounding plating.
On the Portsmouth route, a ro-pax ferry's ballast tanks and fire main gauged during its scheduled maintenance, preparing measured evidence for the annual survey.
Condition gauging of an older chemical tanker at the energy berths for an owner weighing life extension against sale, covering deck, ballast tanks and cargo tanks once gas-free.
Pre-docking gauging of ballast and double-bottom tanks on a container feeder at CSP Bilbao, sent to a northern Spanish yard to prepare the steel list for its renewal survey.

logistics: Technicians reach Bilbao Airport from India via a European hub, or fly into Madrid and continue by domestic flight or road; the outer harbour is reached by road from the city. ISPS access to the terminals is requested by the ship's agent, who can also book a launch for ships lying off the breakwaters. Our technicians travel on Schengen visas, so mobilisation is timed around visa issue and the vessel's expected arrival; winter weather in the Bay of Biscay can shift arrivals, and the plan is kept flexible accordingly.

faqs.q: Is there an emission control area at Bilbao?
faqs.a: Not at present: no SOx ECA covers the Bay of Biscay, and at sea ships use fuel meeting the global sulphur limit. At berth, EU rules require low-sulphur fuel or an accepted equivalent, and ships sailing north reach the North Sea ECA at the approaches to the English Channel. Scrubber piping on ships trading between Bilbao and northern Europe still works hard and is worth gauging on a regular schedule.

faqs.q: Can heavy-weather damage be assessed in Bilbao before the ship sails?
faqs.a: Yes, if the ship's stay allows it. We combine magnetic particle testing at the cracked or suspect details with ultrasonic gauging of the surrounding structure, and report locations, indication lengths and thicknesses so that class and the owner can decide whether a temporary repair, a condition of class or a permanent repair in a yard is appropriate. Early notice helps us reach the ship before it sails.

faqs.q: Can you measure cargo hold structure on a bulk carrier while it discharges in Bilbao?
faqs.a: Holds become accessible as discharge progresses, and with the stevedores' and the chief officer's agreement the technicians can gauge frames, hopper and topside tank boundaries and bulkheads in emptied holds. Longer steel and scrap discharges give room for a systematic programme; on short calls, we concentrate on the areas the coming survey or a known problem requires.

faqs.q: What lead time does thickness measurement in Bilbao need?
faqs.a: As early as the vessel's schedule is known. Our technicians need Schengen visas, and a planned survey or maintenance stop gives time to complete that and agree the measurement plan. Short-notice requests are still worth sending — tell us the berth, the dates and the scope, and we will say honestly whether a team can reach the ship in time.
